questions.q: Why is a covariance matrix Σ always positive semi-definite?
options: Because all its entries are positive numbers
Because for any weight vector w, w^T Σ w equals Var(w^T X), and a variance can never be negative
Because it is always diagonal
Because covariance matrices are defined to only contain zeros and ones
questions.explain: The quadratic form w^T Σ w equals the variance of the weighted combination w^T X, and since variance is never negative, Σ must be positive semi-definite for every w.

questions.q: What does the formula σ_p² = w^T Σ w compute?
options: The expected return of the portfolio
The portfolio's variance, as a quadratic form in the weights
The Sharpe ratio of the portfolio
The number of assets in the portfolio
questions.explain: Portfolio variance is exactly the quadratic form w^T Σ w, which sums w_i * w_j * Σ_ij across every pair of assets.

questions.q: In PCA applied to a covariance matrix Σ = QΛQ^T, what does each eigenvector (column of Q) represent?
options: The average return of all assets
A principal-component portfolio: an uncorrelated combination of the original assets
The risk-free rate
A row of the original data matrix
questions.explain: Each eigenvector defines a portfolio of the original assets; because eigenvectors of a symmetric matrix are orthogonal, these principal-component portfolios are uncorrelated with each other.

questions.q: What does the 'explained variance ratio' of the i-th principal component measure?
options: λ_i divided by trace(Σ), the share of total variance captured by that component
The correlation between component i and component i+1
The number of assets loading on component i
The average of all eigenvalues
questions.explain: The explained variance ratio is λ_i / trace(Σ), since trace(Σ) equals the sum of all eigenvalues, which equals total variance.

questions.q: Why does the guide use np.linalg.eigh rather than np.linalg.eig for a covariance matrix?
options: eigh is faster for any matrix regardless of structure
eigh is written specifically for symmetric matrices and guarantees real eigenvalues and orthonormal eigenvectors
eig cannot compute eigenvalues at all
eigh only works for 2x2 matrices
questions.explain: np.linalg.eigh exploits the guaranteed symmetry of a covariance matrix to return real eigenvalues and orthonormal eigenvectors directly and more reliably than the general-purpose eig.
